evidence:
All 54 criteria (3 gate, 42 functional, 6 polish, 3 visual) were read against the workbook row and skill section 32 (defects: 'looks right', a source read, a response-shape assertion with no state change, or a probe that leaves no trace). The large majority are sound: each names judge-chosen distinctive markers, reads the source/console/library/history back in the browser, and negatives carry a working control (for example cw_stop_cancels_pending_work, cw_newer_run_supersedes, cw_preview_isolation, cw_dynamic_code_refused, cw_run_starts_fresh_document, cw_stale_save_refused); durable state is re-read after storage clearing and restart_app (cw_save_reload_restart, cw_shared_saved_record). No criterion asks for a source read or a response-shape-only assertion. Scripted golden results on these bytes show every criterion id true; that is scripted Playwright, not a judge run on these bytes.

FINDING 1 (Fail, P2) - tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:371, cw_history_restore_retry: 'Send the same already completed restore request again, through the control the app offers for retrying it or, if it offers none, by replaying the recorded request, with its headers, as the application notes allow: no fifth revision may be created.' The preferred path is an app-supplied control, and the only graded observation is an absence (no fifth revision). Nothing tells the judge to confirm that pressing that control actually issued a second restore request, so the probe leaves no trace and a control that sends nothing earns the credit. The public requirement is a server-side property (behaviour.md:13 'If the same restore request is sent again after it was already committed, for example after a lost reply, it must not create another revision'). This conflicts with qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md 'A negative needs a successful control ... A dead feature must not earn credit for doing nothing'. The golden test and the hosted judge on the earlier candidate both used only the app control (persist.cjs:103 clicks 'Retry same restore'; hosted reasoning: 'The app's own Retry same restore control created no new revision (history count unchanged)') and neither recorded that a request was sent. The same sentence also lets the step be dropped entirely ('say so and leave this one step out without failing the criterion for it'), and the replay branch (recording method, path, headers and body with @playwright/mcp 0.0.79 and re-sending by in-page fetch) has no measurement on any candidate: NOT EXERCISED.

FINDING 2 (Note, P3) - tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:32, cw_controls_feedback_and_labels: 'Check that the main controls have understandable visible names ... Fails if a main control has no readable name'. 'Main controls' is not enumerated and 'understandable' is a judgement with no stated observable; an icon-only Undo/Redo with a tooltip or aria-label can be passed or failed by different judges. The other half of the criterion (three actions each give textual feedback) is concrete.

FINDING 3 (Note, P3) - tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:38 and :47, cw_caret_navigation_and_line_numbers and cw_grapheme_navigation_and_deletion: the plain-arrow steps rely on the 'line and column readout' whose base (zero or one based, graphemes or UTF-16 units) is not public (ui.md:5 only says 'the current line and column'). The criteria do not state a base, so a consistent judge can decide them, and the Shift+Arrow copy and Backspace/Delete steps give durable evidence; the hosted judge on the earlier candidate read 'Col1->2->4->5->7->8' and passed. Residual risk only.

FINDING 4 (Note, P3) - tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:326, cw_preview_isolation: the fetch probes are decided by a log line written from an asynchronous catch; if neither a resolved nor a rejected line ever appears, the listed fail conditions ('if a fetch from the preview resolves') are not met and the step passes on silence. The synchronous own-preview marker is the only logging control.

Visual likert criteria are craft ratings with described anchors and are judged on the shipped format, not reported here.
counterexample: Weak app that passes: the server appends a revision on every POST restore with no operation id or base-revision check, so a replay after a lost reply creates a duplicate revision, violating behaviour.md:13. The client shows a 'Retry restore' button that only re-sends when the previous attempt failed (or is simply a no-op after a completed restore). The judge restores revision one (revision four appears), presses 'Retry restore', sees four revisions, and credits the idempotency step; the criterion's remaining steps also pass because history is append-only. Full credit of weight 1.5 is given although the graded promise is not implemented. Conversely, a conforming app with no retry control depends on the unmeasured replay branch: if the judge cannot recover the recorded body and headers (for example a client-generated operation id) and re-sends an approximation, a correct server legitimately treats it as a new restore and adds a fifth revision, failing a conforming app.
suggested_fix: In cw_history_restore_retry require positive evidence of the repeat: after using the app's retry control the judge must see, in the browser's recorded network activity, a second restore request with the same method and path as the first (or an explicit visible confirmation from the app that the repeat was received); if no second request is seen, fall back to replaying the recorded request, and only then judge 'no fifth revision'. Optionally name the controls meant by 'main controls' in cw_controls_feedback_and_labels and say that a tooltip or accessible name alone does or does not count.
